messages:
santiago: Thanks everyone for joining the all-hands earlier. Quick follow-up thread for infra questions I promised I'd track.

maya: Awesome — can you restate the GPU shipment ETA? I missed the exact week.

santiago: Sure. Short version: vendor confirmed first rack shipment arriving week of May 12, broader shipments ramping throughout June. That's for the new A100 pool in us-west-2 and eu-west-1.

oliver: Are those racks immediately usable for Dedicated customers or do they go into a warm pool first?

santiago: They'll land into our onboarding pool. Plan is: validate health -> apply our kernel configs/firmware -> join as capacity with annotation dedicated=false by default. We can earmark specific racks to Dedicated if sales/ops request and we commit.

lisa: Question about regions: will ap-southeast be in the first wave or later?

santiago: APAC (ap-southeast-1) is targeted for the second wave in June — depends on customs/lighting tests. If we get a green light earlier we'll accelerate but don't rely on it for early June.

cecilia: How will autoscaling behave with the new capacity? Any changes to burst rules / priority tiers?

maya: We pushed an autoscaler PR that adds a "burstable" bool per capacity pool. TL;DR: default behavior unchanged, but burstable pools can accept short-lived jobs up to 2x for 90s while we spin up reserved nodes.

santiago: To add: policy will prefer Dedicated pools first for committed customers, then fall back to burstable public pools. There is an explicit cap per-tenant so bursts can't starve scheduled fleets.

oliver: Can we see the new policy snippet? Gives me more confidence for routing logic.

maya: pasted config below (internal syntax):

```
capacity_pools:
  - name: prod-dedicated
    tier: reserved
    prioritize: true
  - name: shared-burstable
    tier: burst
    burstable: true
    burst_cooldown: 90s
    tenant_cap: 0.2 # max 20% of pool per tenant
```

lisa: Nice. Who is owning the rollout and monitoring for regressions?

santiago: Eng-platform owns rollout + canary plan. Eng-sre is co-owner for alerts and incident playbooks. Maya will drive the rollout schedule with me.

maya: We'll do a 48hr canary on non-critical namespaces, then open to low-volume Dedicated accounts, then full ramp. Monitoring: token latency p95, queue-length, cold-start rate.

cecilia: Any changes to the fallback logic if a region can't take traffic (e.g., regulatory or outage)?

santiago: Yes — new routing policy supports region blacklists per-tenant. If a region is disallowed or down, traffic gets routed to nearest allowed region respecting cost tier and latency SLOs. We also added a "graceful-degrade" model fallback to smaller quantized variants.

oliver: Will the graceful-degrade models be enabled by default?

maya: Not by default. It's opt-in per route for now. We're measuring quality delta to define safe autopromote thresholds.

lisa: Action items I noted:
- maya: finalize autoscaler PR + add tenant_cap defaults (due Apr 30)
- eng-platform: canary plan doc and schedule (due May 5)
- ops: confirm customs / datacenter ETA for ap-southeast (due Apr 28)

santiago: Exactly. I'll ping sales for any immediate Dedicated customer requests that need pre-necking racks.

ops-bot: [automated] link to canary doc: https://redwood.internal/docs/canary-autoscale-v2 (access: eng-platform, eng-sre, infra)

maya: One more note — if teams have latency-sensitive workloads, flag them in the canary doc so we can include them in targeted tests.

cecilia: I'll collate flagged services by EOD Friday and drop them here.

oliver: Can we get a short Slack thread next week to confirm actual rack arrival? I want to plan migration windows.

santiago: Yes — I'll start a "rack-arrivals" thread when we get tracking numbers. For now, assume May 12 for first shipment and treat all dates as tentative.

lisa: Thanks — this is super helpful. I'll update the all-hands follow-up doc with these action items and deadlines.

santiago: Thanks team. If anyone has other Qs, drop them here and we'll fold into the rollout doc.
